_provenance.method: per-team season ratings recovered by least squares from rating_diff, identified up to an additive constant
_provenance.unblocked: The direct test was recorded as impossible because CFBD is unreachable. cfbfastR play-by-play on GitHub is reachable and carries per-team player names, so returning production was computed the same way as for the NFL. Usage aggregates committed at model/cfb_usage/ (352 KB).

verdict: CFB's returning-production discount is VINDICATED where NFL's was rejected: significant interaction, monotonic terciles, and it improves held-out ordering. Unchanged anyway -- the scale fix (under-shrinks by ~15%) gates at t=1.93, just short. Re-run when 2024-2025 are in the walk-forward cache.
next_test: extend cfb_full_walk_forward_cache.csv to 2024-2025; two more transitions gates the rescale

returning_production_test.vs_nfl: NFL: interaction -0.13 (t -0.38), non-monotonic, and returning DEGRADED rank correlation .433->.399. CFB: +0.60 (t +2.13), monotonic, and it IMPROVES rank .400->.419. Roughly 40% annual roster churn against roughly 10%.
